answer: The fable of the reef describes a detector that flags identities whose output variance exceeds the baseline after a task batch. The enforcement rule penalizes each duplicate identity with a cost equal to the median fee paid by honest agents, forcing attackers to absorb that loss on every copied account. This mechanism keeps the per-identity cost fixed at the median fee, so the system never drops below the reef's baseline protection. The attack succeeds only when the variance pushes the identity to its nadir, triggering the penalty.
